## Quarterly Report of the Harbour Authority

## 1. Operations

Environmental monitoring continued at all six stations. Average water temperature was 14.8 degrees Celsius; dissolved oxygen remained within the permitted range throughout the quarter, and no exceedances of the turbidity limit were recorded.

The board approved a revised tariff schedule that takes effect on the first of July. Dues for vessels under 5,000 gross tonnes are unchanged, while larger ships pay a surcharge of 1.5 percent to fund the dredging programme in the approach channel.

The harbour authority published its quarterly report on Tuesday. Cargo volumes rose by 4.2 percent compared with the same period last year, driven mainly by container traffic from the northern routes. Bulk shipments of grain fell slightly after a dry summer.

## 2. Finance

Passenger numbers recovered strongly. Ferry services carried 1,284,000 passengers, the highest figure since records began, and the new evening sailing to Westport proved popular with commuters who previously relied on the coastal road.

Environmental monitoring continued at all six stations. Average water temperature was 14.8 degrees Celsius; dissolved oxygen remained within the permitted range throughout the quarter, and no exceedances of the turbidity limit were recorded.

Maintenance of the eastern breakwater is scheduled to begin in March. The work will close berths 7 and 8 for about six weeks; vessels will be redirected to the western terminal, where two additional cranes were commissioned in January.

## Key points

• Cargo volumes rose by 4.2 percent.
• Berths 7 and 8 close for six weeks from March.
• A revised tariff schedule starts on 1 July.
